past_medical_history: Obstructive sleep apnoea, CPAP prescribed 6 years ago, used inconsistently
family_history: Mother had a stroke at 74 and died at 79

social_history.living_situation: Lives alone since her husband died 3 years ago; a daughter visits daily
social_history.driving: Stopped driving two years ago by her own choice

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person and place, gives the year correctly but the month as two months earlier. MoCA 20/30, losing points on trail-making, digit span backwards, serial sevens, verbal fluency (9 animals) and delayed recall (3/5 unaided, 5/5 with cues). Marked psychomotor slowing. Affect flat rather than sad; she denies sadness and says she simply cannot be bothered.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full. Visual fields full to confrontation. Mild bilateral hypomimia. Speech mildly dysarthric with imprecise consonants. Palate symmetric, tongue midline.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk. Tone mildly increased in both legs. Strength 5/5 throughout. No drift, no tremor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch, pinprick, vibration and proprioception throughout.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 3+ at the knees, 2+ elsewhere. Plantar responses flexor. Palmomental reflex present.
neurological_exam.coordination: Intact finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin. No dysmetria.
neurological_exam.gait: Cautious, short-stepped, mildly wide-based with preserved arm swing. Turns en bloc in four steps. Tandem impossible. Romberg negative.
neurological_exam.additional: No resting tremor, no rigidity at the wrists. Glabellar tap unsuppressed. Nocturia three times nightly. Epworth Sleepiness Scale 13/24 with inconsistent CPAP use.

patient.chief_complaint: Eighteen months of slowing, apathy and forgetfulness that her daughter says is not depression
patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Renata Bosco is a 71-year-old retired ward clerk who attends with her daughter for evaluation of 18 months of cognitive decline. The daughter's account is that her mother 'stopped starting things'. She used to cook every day and telephone her grandchildren; now she sits in the same chair for most of the afternoon, the fridge holds expired food, and she has to be prompted to shower. She is not sad, does not cry, denies hopelessness and sleeps rather too much than too little. Her general practitioner started sertraline eight months ago on the assumption of a depressive episode; there has been no change in eight months at a therapeutic dose. Cognitively the daughter reports slowness rather than forgetting: her mother eventually recalls conversations and appointments, particularly when reminded of the context, but cannot follow a recipe with several steps, has twice left the gas ring on, and now takes an hour to do what used to take fifteen minutes. She has stopped managing her own bank card. There have been no discrete episodes of weakness or speech difficulty, no falls, no visual hallucinations, no fluctuation in alertness and no dream enactment. She continues to smoke fifteen cigarettes a day, and her blood pressure has been between 150 and 170 systolic at every recorded visit for the past two years. She uses her CPAP machine perhaps two nights a week.

findings.type: White matter hyperintensity of presumed vascular origin
findings.location: Confluent periventricular and deep white matter, frontal predominant

signal_characteristics.T2_FLAIR: Confluent caps and rims with beginning confluence of deep foci, frontal predominance

findings.location: Right corona radiata, left putamen, right centrum semiovale
Bilateral basal ganglia and centrum semiovale

signal_characteristics.T2: Linear CSF-signal spaces along the perforating vessels

findings.location: Mild global, medial temporal lobes preserved

additional_observations: SWI shows no microbleeds and no cortical superficial siderosis
No restricted diffusion — all lesions chronic
No cortical infarct in any arterial territory
No mass, no hydrocephalus, no abnormal enhancement
mri.impression: Severe sporadic small-vessel disease with confluent frontal-predominant white matter hyperintensity (Fazekas 3), three chronic lacunes and moderately enlarged perivascular spaces. No microbleeds, no cortical infarcts, medial temporal lobes preserved. The burden accounts for the frontal-subcortical syndrome.

labs.interpretation: LDL 142 mg/dL is well above target for a patient with established cerebrovascular disease. HbA1c 5.9% indicates impaired glucose regulation without diabetes. TSH, B12, folate, RPR and HIV are normal or negative. There is no anaemia and renal function is preserved.

specialized_test.impression: Executive dysfunction and slowed processing with intact recognition memory, and performance-validity measures passed — the deficit is genuine and not effort-dependent, which is the distinction that matters when depression has been assumed.

findings.performance: Digit span backwards 0/1, serial sevens 3/3 with long latency — impaired efficiency
Severely slowed on every timed item
Delayed recall 3/5 unaided, 5/5 cued — retrieval pattern
Mild dysarthria; naming and comprehension intact

clinical_assessment.impression: MoCA 20/30 with executive dysfunction, marked psychomotor slowing and fully cue-responsive recall. The Apathy Evaluation Scale is clinically elevated at 48 while the Geriatric Depression Scale is 4/15, and eight months of sertraline at a therapeutic dose produced no change: this is the frontal-subcortical apathy of small-vessel disease, not a depressive episode.

output.impression: Timed-up-and-go 15.9 s with a cautious, short-stepped, mildly wide-based gait and preserved arm swing. The pattern is the higher-level gait disorder of small-vessel disease; there is no magnetic quality and no freezing.

background.posterior_dominant_rhythm: 9 Hz, symmetric, reactive to eye opening

eeg.impression: Normal awake EEG for age. No epileptiform discharges and no focal or generalised slowing.

labs.interpretation: The additional panels requested are negative and do not contribute to the diagnosis in this presentation.

findings.signal: study performed and reported as non-contributory
findings.description: no finding relevant to this presentation

advanced_imaging.impression: The study was performed and does not contribute to the diagnosis in this presentation.

additional_observations: Chronic ischaemic white matter change, better characterised on the MRI already obtained
ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No haemorrhage, mass or hydrocephalus. CT cannot exclude microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis.

findings: No intracardiac thrombus, vegetation or shunt. No pericardial effusion.
No atrial fibrillation. No pauses. No AV block.

vascular_cognitive_impairment.query: vascular cognitive impairment diagnostic criteria and secondary prevention

results.title: Diagnostic criteria for vascular cognitive disorders: a VASCOG statement
results.authors: Sachdev P, Kalaria R, O'Brien J, et al.
results.summary: Requires a cognitive syndrome documented on a validated instrument plus imaging or temporal evidence that cerebrovascular disease accounts for it.

results.title: Neuroimaging standards for research into small vessel disease (STRIVE-2)
results.authors: Duering M, Biessels GJ, Brodtmann A, et al.
results.summary: Defines and standardises the reporting of white matter hyperintensity, lacunes, microbleeds, perivascular spaces and cortical superficial siderosis.

vascular_cognitive_impairment.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for vascular cognitive impairment; management is control of the vascular risk factors, secondary prevention matched to the mechanism, review of the anticholinergic burden, and treatment of coexisting Alzheimer pathology where biomarkers support it.

medication_review.proposed: review of the current medication list for anticholinergic burden
warnings: Anticholinergic load is a reversible contributor to cognitive impairment in this population and should be quantified before any new prescription.
medication_review.summary: No prohibitive interaction identified within the current list.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Vascular dementia — subcortical ischaemic (small-vessel) type, with frontal-subcortical apathy previously misattributed to depression

differential.key_features: Apathy without sadness, a Geriatric Depression Scale of 4/15, an Apathy Evaluation Scale of 48, no response to eight months of therapeutic sertraline, and passed performance-validity measures place this below the vascular explanation
Recall is fully cue-responsive, the medial temporal lobes are preserved, and the deficit is dominated by slowing rather than forgetting
Poor CPAP adherence with an Epworth of 13 is a genuine contributor worth correcting, but it does not explain a Fazekas 3 white matter burden or the loss of instrumental independence
Apathy is prominent but there is no disinhibition, no loss of empathy, no compulsivity, no dietary change and no frontotemporal atrophy
Evans index 0.26 with no ventriculomegaly and no magnetic gait

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a collateral history from an informant who sees the patient daily: the shape of the decline (abrupt, stepwise or gradual), whether any step can be dated to a cerebrovascular event, and which instrumental activities have been lost
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Insidious rather than stepwise decline with apathy and psychomotor slowing out of proportion to memory loss, no response to eight months of adequately dosed antidepressant, and loss of instrumental independence corroborated by the informant

optimal_actions.action: Perform a validated bedside cognitive assessment and record the per-domain profile and whether delayed recall improves with cueing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: MoCA 20/30 with executive and processing-speed impairment, fully cue-responsive recall, and apathy dissociated from depression on formal scales

optimal_actions.action: Order the reversible-cause screen and the vascular-risk assays that will be treated (CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, RPR, HIV, HbA1c, lipid panel)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Reversible causes excluded; LDL 142 mg/dL and prediabetic HbA1c 5.9% identify the untreated vascular substrate alongside her continued smoking

optimal_actions.action: Perform timed gait and balance testing: the short-stepped, wide-based gait with preserved arm swing is part of the subcortical syndrome and separates it from the gait of normal pressure hydrocephalus and of parkinsonian disorders
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Timed-up-and-go 15.9 s with a short-stepped wide-based gait, preserved arm swing and dual-task deterioration

optimal_actions.action: Obtain brain MRI reported in STRIVE-2 terms — FLAIR for white matter hyperintensity with a Fazekas grade, T1/T2 for lacunes, DWI to establish that the lesions are chronic, and SWI for microbleeds and cortical superficial siderosis — together with the medial temporal atrophy grade
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confluent frontal-predominant white matter hyperintensity (Fazekas 3) with three chronic lacunes and preserved medial temporal lobes — a small-vessel burden matching the frontal-subcortical presentation

optimal_actions.action: Order formal multi-domain neuropsychological testing to settle the executive-versus-amnestic attribution and to document a baseline for follow-up
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Frontal-subcortical profile with preserved recognition memory; formal testing confirms the deficit is not effort-dependent

optimal_actions.action: Confirm the diagnostic criteria applied and the current secondary-prevention targets against the guidelines
optimal_actions.expected_finding: VASCOG 2014 criteria and the 2021 AHA/ASA secondary prevention targets confirmed

optimal_actions.action: Review the medication list for anticholinergic burden and for the interaction between antithrombotic choice and the microbleed burden before prescribing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Anticholinergic contributors identified and the antithrombotic choice reconciled with the imaging burden

optimal_actions.action: Treat the vascular substrate and the two reversible contributors: antihypertensive intensification to a systolic target below 130 mmHg, high-intensity statin to an LDL below 70 mg/dL, structured smoking cessation, and CPAP adherence support; taper the sertraline that has produced no benefit rather than escalating it
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Blood pressure, lipids, smoking and CPAP adherence addressed as the modifiable drivers; the ineffective antidepressant reviewed rather than escalated

optimal_actions.action: Disclose the diagnosis and its mechanism to the patient and the informant, and address driving, medication management, finances, advance care planning and caregiver support
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Patient and informant engaged in care planning; safety domains addressed

useless_tools.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role in vascular cognitive impairment; it belongs to the differential of a rapidly progressive or fluctuating course (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, non-convulsive status, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy), none of which is present here

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
Cardiac sympathetic imaging is a test for dementia with Lewy bodies and for autonomic failure; it says nothing about cerebrovascular disease

An untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery in a chronic stepwise decline with a hypertensive imaging burden is the archetypal expensive miss; the indication for those assays is a subacute multidomain syndrome
The MRI already obtained answers everything a CT could and more: CT cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis, so it cannot grade the vascular burden this diagnosis rests on
There is no embolic lesion pattern to explain: the burden here is small-vessel, and a structural cardioembolic source would not account for it
Prolonged rhythm monitoring is for an unexplained embolic infarct pattern; in pure small-vessel disease it changes nothing about the diagnosis or the treatment

sequence_constraints.reason: Document the cognitive deficit before attributing it: imaging read without a cognitive profile invites over-attribution of incidental white matter change

critical_actions: Distinguish apathy from depression formally rather than assuming the antidepressant failed for want of dose
Document the cognitive deficit on a validated instrument and record cue-responsiveness of recall
Exclude the reversible causes of cognitive impairment with the named screen
Obtain brain MRI with SWI and grade the small-vessel burden in STRIVE-2 terms
Confirm the deficit is genuine with performance-validity measures where a psychiatric attribution has already been made
Address smoking, blood pressure, lipids and CPAP adherence — the only interventions that alter the course
Assess home safety, including the gas ring and medication management
contraindicated_actions: Do not escalate or switch antidepressants on the assumption of treatment-resistant depression before the vascular diagnosis is considered
Do not prescribe anticholinergic or sedating agents (first-generation antihistamines, tricyclics, benzodiazepines) in a patient with small-vessel disease and falls risk
Do not start an antipsychotic for apathy
Do not accept 'she is just depressed' as the endpoint of the assessment when instrumental independence has been lost
key_reasoning_points: Apathy and depression are dissociable and the distinction is measurable: an elevated Apathy Evaluation Scale with a low Geriatric Depression Scale and no response to an adequate antidepressant trial points to frontal-subcortical disease

An insidious rather than stepwise course does not argue against small-vessel disease — progressive confluent white matter change produces gradual decline, and only the multi-infarct mechanism is characteristically stepwise
Performance-validity measures matter once a psychiatric attribution has been made, because they are what distinguish a genuine deficit from an effort-dependent one
Smoking and untreated hypertension are the two drivers here and both are modifiable; no additional imaging changes management
Poor CPAP adherence is a real contributor to cognitive impairment and should be corrected, but it cannot be the whole explanation in the presence of a Fazekas 3 burden

red_herrings.data_point: Eight months of sertraline for presumed depression
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the assessment on a psychiatric diagnosis and invites a change of antidepressant instead of a dementia workup
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: An adequately dosed antidepressant trial that produced no change in eight months, with apathy dissociated from low mood on formal scales, argues against depression as the explanation

red_herrings.data_point: Epworth Sleepiness Scale 13 with poor CPAP use
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests untreated sleep apnoea as the sole cause of the cognitive complaint
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Sleep apnoea is a genuine contributor and should be treated, but it does not produce a Fazekas 3 white matter burden or explain lost instrumental independence

key_educational_points: Frontal-subcortical apathy in small-vessel disease is routinely misdiagnosed as depression; the scales dissociate them
A gradual course is compatible with small-vessel vascular dementia — stepwise decline is a feature of the multi-infarct mechanism, not of every vascular dementia
Performance-validity measures belong in the battery whenever a psychiatric explanation has already been applied
Smoking cessation and blood-pressure control are the treatment; there is no disease-modifying drug
metadata.revision_reason: authored on the July 2026 clinical tool review — vascular dementia replaces peripheral neuropathy
metadata.difficulty_rationale: Severe unambiguous small-vessel burden; the difficulty lies only in overriding an existing psychiatric label, and the formal scales resolve it
